title: AI candidate evidence-semantic contract clause
description: One field, one candidate clause. Reuses the canonical evidence-state alphabet from research/evidence_semantics/EVIDENCE_SEMANTICS_CONTRACT.schema.json rather than defining a second ontology (item 12). Every semantic claim carries a citation; a claim with no citation is UNSUPPORTED_INFERENCE by construction, not by judgement.

abstain.description: true when the visible evidence does not support any clause. A correct abstention is a good answer, not a failure.

explicit_semantic_state_found.description: the primary decision. NO_... is first-class: most protocol fields have no sentinel.

clauses.description: individual semantic claims, each independently citable and independently scorable

state.description: canonical evidence state, where the clause names one

support.description: citations. EMPTY means the clause is unsupported and the validator will mark it so.

locator.description: file:line, file:line-line, or schema path such as common.xml:BATTERY_STATUS.current_battery

quote.description: text the validator must find at that locator. This is what makes grounding checkable rather than asserted.

support_kind.description: precedence tier from the prompt's evidence hierarchy

confidence.description: RANKING ONLY. Item 14: confidence must never gate a safety decision. Nothing in this package reads this field except the ranking and the high-confidence-unsupported metric.

contract_status.description: the candidate's OWN self-report. The deterministic validator assigns the real status independently and may disagree; disagreement is itself a measurement.
